comparator.academicYear: Revised curriculum applicable from 2023-2024 (official programme page and outline, checked 2026-09-30); year 1 course credits confirmed in the 2025-2026 Faculty of Law course descriptions and year 2 and year 3 credits taken from the 2024-2025 Faculty of Law curriculum archive, the latest edition that lists them
comparator.sourceNotes: Reconstructed from the official Maastricht University programme page 'Courses & curriculum' (s0), which states that the revised curriculum outline applies from 2023-2024 and publishes it as an outline image (s2). The outline names every compulsory course and skills track in years 1 and 2 and, in year 3, eight elective places (two in each of periods 1, 2, 4 and 5) and a Final Legal Challenge / Bachelor's Essay. It prints no EC values. EC values come from the Faculty of Law course descriptions: year 1 from the 2025-2026 edition (s3: Constitutional Law, Introduction to Private Law, International and European Law and Foundations of Law 11 EC each; Skills I and II 8 EC each) and year 2 and the Bachelor's Essay from the 2024-2025 archive edition (s4: Private Law and Law of the European Union 11 EC each; Criminal Law, Philosophy of Private Law, Criminal Procedure, Administrative Law and Conflict Prevention and Resolution 6 EC each; Legal Research 8 EC; Bachelor's Essay ELS 12 EC). The compulsory courses of years 1 and 2 total 120 EC (60 EC each). Year 3 therefore holds the remaining 60 EC: the 12-EC essay plus 48 EC for the eight elective places, i.e. 6 EC each, the standard EC of the elective courses in the archive; this allocation is derived by arithmetic from the outline and the archive, not printed in a single official table. The revised programme's elective offer is governed by the Elective Education Regulations and is not enumerated on the pages checked, so the elective space is kept as one explicit open component rather than filled with named courses; the archive's own elective list still describes the unrevised programme. The zero-EC English Language Proficiency requirement (LAW1201) is not a credit-bearing component and is omitted from the 180 EC. The programme page names no formal route, track or specialisation for the Bachelor European Law School; the Spanish and European law dual degree named in some registry interest rows is a separate programme not described on these pages.

alternatives.concept: The strongest defensible UCR response to the Bachelor European Law School at Maastricht University, whose curriculum combines multi-level constitutional, international and EU law, comparative private law, the foundations of law, criminal and administrative law and a skills track in legal reasoning, research and conflict resolution. UCR's seven law courses carry the core: a general introduction to law, human rights, criminal law, public international law, comparative constitutional and administrative law, comparative private law and EU law. Political science, philosophy, history, economics, rhetoric, logic and research courses make specific complementary contributions to the EU and international order, the foundations of law and the argumentation and research strands; they do not replace legal training that UCR does not offer, such as criminal procedure, legal research and writing or specialist private and EU law.

alternatives.concept: A genuinely different route built on the target's stated interest in law and contemporary social problems and on the legal challenges and electives of the European Law School that address inequality, access to justice, crime and punishment, artificial intelligence, environmental protection through international law and human-rights organisations. Instead of following the doctrinal sequence of constitutional, private and EU law, it studies law as a social institution and a means of pursuing justice: human rights, criminal justice, public international law, constitutional rights and EU fundamental rights, together with sociology, social movements, ethics, political conflict, colonial history, AI ethics, race and the economics of inequality and redistribution.

The label names the legal core (human rights and criminal justice) and the sociological and inequality strands that give the programme its social-change orientation, without implying a full law degree or a pure sociology programme.
alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Alternative 1 organises the programme around the target's doctrinal core: comparative private law, EU law and institutions, international relations and the foundations of law (history, economics), supported by rhetoric and argumentation training. Alternative 2 changes the organising priority from doctrinal breadth to the social problems that law addresses, following the direct programme interest 'law and contemporary social problems' and the target's social-problem legal challenges. It drops ten Alternative 1 courses (Principles of Private Law, European Union Politics, Theory of International Relations, Modern History, Introduction to Economics, The Art of Rhetorical Communication, Rhetoric in Action, Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Calling Bullshit and History Research Seminar) and adds ten courses that Alternative 1 does not contain: four sociology courses (Introduction to Sociology, Modern Sociology, Social Movements & Environmental Justice, New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory), History of Empires, Histories of Gender, AI Ethics, Media & Race, Research Methods & Statistics and Public Economics. The two programmes share 14 courses, including the core public-law and human-rights courses, and the 10 different courses follow directly from the change in organising priority.

progressionAssessment.rationale: Law, Society & Justice, the formal prerequisite of five law courses, is scheduled in semester 1, so every dependent law course follows it (Comparative Constitutional Law and Introduction to Public International Law in semester 2, Principles of Private Law and Criminal Law & Criminal Justice in semester 3, Foundations of European Union Law in semester 4). Human Rights: Law & Philosophy, Introduction to Political Philosophy and the rhetoric introduction come before Persuasive Communication (semester 5), which builds on rhetoric and argumentation theory. Comparative Politics and Ethics come before the international-relations, EU-politics and peace-and-conflict courses. The 300-level History Research Seminar is placed last, after the other research and argumentation courses.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two UCR alternatives are defensible and production stopped at two. Alternative 1 owns ten generator-eligible rows that describe the target's own core (5807 to 5810 on the interaction of European, international and national law, comparing legal systems, EU law and international law; 5813 on legal history and philosophy; 5816 to 5818 on legal reasoning, finding and evaluating legal sources and legal research and writing; and 5822 and 5825 on independent research and research projects on European legal questions). Alternative 2 is built on the single direct programme-interest row 5815 (law and contemporary social problems), a coherent direction in its own right that the target's legal challenges and electives corroborate; it supplies a different set of ten courses and shares 14 courses with Alternative 1, so it passes the 30 EC / 4 course floor in both directions. The candidate direction 'Negotiation, mediation, dispute resolution and moot-court advocacy' (rows 5819, 5820 and 5821) is supported by the target's Conflict Prevention and Resolution course and Moot Court Training, but it cannot be built into a third valid and coherent UCR programme: UCR's only negotiation course (Negotiation & Strategic Thinking) and only dispute-resolution content (Transnational Business Law) each sit behind a business gateway course (Research Methods & Statistics, Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations) whose content does not serve the concept, UCR has no mediation course, and advocacy is reachable only through generic rhetoric courses already used in Alternative 1, so the differing courses would be an assortment rather than an organising logic. The Spanish law direction (rows 5823 and 5824) belongs to the separate Spanish and European law dual degree; the official pages for this target do not describe it and UCR offers no Spanish law, so it is rejected for insufficient evidence.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Foundations of Law teaches legal history, legal philosophy and law and economics as the foundations of positive law; UCR has no jurisprudence or legal-history course, and Ethics, Introduction to Political Philosophy, Modern History and Introduction to Economics contribute related perspectives without directly addressing the legal-historical, legal-philosophical or economic-analysis-of-law content of the component.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Philosophy of Private Law applies normative theories of justice to private-law doctrines; Ethics teaches the general normative theories but no UCR course addresses private-law doctrine from a philosophical standpoint, so the relationship is contextual.

Comparative Constitutional Law covers the institutions of government, limits on government power, guarantees of rights and judicial review across five legal systems, the subject of Constitutional Law; it is narrower on European and international constitutionalism and adds administrative law.

Introduction to Public International Law covers the sources, subjects and organisation of international law, the use of force and treaty compliance, the international-law half of International and European Law; the EU half is aligned separately with Law of the European Union.

Foundations of European Union Law covers the EU institutional framework, legal order, fundamental rights, citizenship and free movement, the subject of Law of the European Union at a more introductory level.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Administrative Law is a dedicated second-year course; Comparative Constitutional Law, the only UCR course with administrative-law content, is already the strongest counterpart to Constitutional Law and no other scheduled UCR course addresses administrative decision-making or judicial protection against administrative action.
Principles of Private Law covers property, tort and contract law comparatively across several legal systems, the subject of Introduction to Private Law (family law is not named in its description).

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Private Law is the second-year continuation of Introduction to Private Law; UCR offers a single private-law course, which is already the strongest counterpart to Introduction to Private Law, and no other scheduled UCR course addresses private law.
Criminal Law & Criminal Justice covers criminal accountability, the legality principle, justifications and excuses and the justification of punishment, the subject of Criminal Law.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Criminal Procedure covers investigative measures, pre-trial detention, prosecution and the criminal trial from a comparative perspective; Criminal Law & Criminal Justice is already the counterpart to Criminal Law and does not teach criminal procedure.

Peace & Conflict covers theories of conflict causation, conflict transformation and peacebuilding, which corresponds to the conflict-theory part of Conflict Prevention and Resolution; it does not cover negotiation, mediation exercises or the moot court.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Introduction to Law and Legal Reasoning trains study skills, problem-based learning, legal source-finding, case briefing with the IRAC method and a drafting challenge; Personal & Professional Development and Law, Society & Justice do not teach these legal-skills functions, and Calling Bullshit is only a generic source-evaluation counterpart.

The Art of Rhetorical Communication teaches the theory of rhetoric and argumentation, which corresponds to the legal-argumentation part of Thinking Like a Lawyer (structure and evaluation of arguments, persuasion); it does not teach legal syllogisms, the legal challenge or legal reasoning and covers only part of the component's scope.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: Legal Research trains legal research methodology, critical reading of legal sources and academic legal writing; History Research Seminar, Qualitative Research Methodology and Research Methods & Statistics teach research in other disciplines and are only generic transferable research training.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the Final Legal Challenge / Bachelor's Essay is an independent legal-research component; no scheduled UCR course is a bachelor thesis, so the standardized optional independent research element occupies this row.

Explicitly unmatched after semantic review: the eight year-3 elective places are open elective space whose content the revised programme does not enumerate on the checked pages; no scheduled UCR course is aligned with them.

notes.text: The Bachelor European Law School includes a more extensive sequence in private law, EU law, criminal procedure, administrative law and legal research and writing. At UCR, students can study constitutional, private, criminal, international and EU law, but UCR does not offer the same depth or sequence in law.

The Bachelor European Law School organises study around a structured sequence of compulsory law courses and a parallel skills-and-legal-challenge track, followed by a year of electives and a bachelor's essay. At UCR, comparable subjects are distributed across courses in law, political science, philosophy, history and sociology. The UCR programme therefore covers related territory through a different curricular structure rather than reproducing the external programme course by course.
